expectations.evidence: response.md D1: 'Use the nested ObservationCollection only for bulk ingest. For reads, serve /stations, /stations/{code}/sampling-points, a flat, paginated /observations?station=&pollutant=&from=&to=', motivated by about 21 million a year.

expectations.text: The generated JSON Schema is a valid JSON Schema and allows null for the observation value
expectations.evidence: Ran jsonschema Draft202012Validator.check_schema on generated/airquality.schema.json: OK. Instance with value null: 0 errors (value type [number, null]).

expectations.text: The JSON Schema keeps the observation value required but nullable, matching the XSD where the element is mandatory but nillable
expectations.evidence: Observation required includes 'value'; value type [number, null]. Tested: null is valid; key removed gives "'value' is a required property".

expectations.text: An XSD generated from the canonical model accepts the same documents as the original 2.1 XSD: a sample delivery valid against observations.xsd also validates against the generated XSD (checked with lxml)
expectations.evidence: lxml (python -I): examples/sample.xml validates against the original (True) and generated/observations.xsd (True); a self-written minimal doc with nil value, validity 0, verification 7, no offset and an odd pollutant is also valid in both. A lat=95 doc is accepted by both (no tightening).

expectations.text: The pollutant code list is linked to a named standard vocabulary (e.g. the EEA/Eionet air quality pollutant vocabulary) with its register URI and a snapshot date or version, or reusing such a vocabulary is recommended to the user with the reason
expectations.evidence: The model has no vocabulary link for pollutant (only the description copied from the XSD). xsd-review.md Q5 cites http://dd.eionet.europa.eu/vocabulary/aq/pollutant/ only to note its numeric identifiers; the recommendation is to 'map them to a controlled list' and 'add them as an enum in the model', not to reuse or link the EEA vocabulary. No snapshot date or version. D3 lists 'code-list URIs for pollutant' only as a future partner-schema proposal, with no reason given.

notes: Iteration 2 assertions discriminate much better than iteration 1: new-model 14 vs 11, amend 14 vs 12, xsd 13 vs 9 (iteration 1: 11 vs 10, 10 vs 10, 10 vs 8).

Still partly method-encoded: single source of truth, volumes in the model and vocabulary checks reward the skill's approach; on some substance the baseline was stronger (tree: trigger-filled location history, exchange-schema business rules, full legacy migration script; xsd: clearer API read-model note).

Skill/tool issues found: (1) dmtool reads compatibility.projection from the old release, so a model released without it can never get the minor bump; (2) a scope:all constraint on a brand-new attribute is reported as breaking; (3) amend run kept model.version at 1.0.0 while drafting, so preview exports carry the old $id; (4) xsd run's generated XSD tightened lat/lon ranges — disclosed, but not caught by the single-sample compatibility assertion.

Assertion gaps to fix: XSD compatibility should test edge-case documents; location-history check should require automatic capture; add checks for exchange-schema business rules and migration safety (additive only); generator assertion partly measures tool availability.
Cost: with-skill runs used more tokens on average but were faster in wall time (baseline mean inflated by the 534 s tree run).
